question: At what latitude does the easterly jet stream blow over peninsular India during the summer months?
solution:
The correct answer is __**14o**N__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The easterly jet stream over Peninsular India during the summer months typically blows around the 14°N latitude.
 
• This jet stream, known as the Tropical Easterly Jet (TEJ), is a low-level jet stream that flows from the east to west during the summer and plays an important role in the monsoon dynamics.
 
• The easterly jet stream is located at an altitude of around 10 km above the surface, and it is stronger during the summer months when the monsoon winds are active.
 
• The jet stream is found mainly over Peninsular India and parts of the Bay of Bengal at around 14°N latitude.
 
• The position of the easterly jet can influence the intensity and onset of the Indian summer monsoon.
